governanceNotes: D1 batch 49 (2026-09-24): deferred. Zero-record screen recorded 2026-09-24: the located jersey-finger literature reports functional and complication outcomes rather than a catalog-fit secondary diagnosis - the Tempelaere 2017 series of 29 patients reported Buck-Gramcko grades (six excellent, six good, seven satisfactory, ten poor), a mean QuickDASH of 5.66, and twelve complications in nine patients without itemising a musculoskeletal secondary diagnosis, and the Poggetti 2025 comparative study of 66 patients with type II Leddy and Packer avulsions addressed total active motion, time to recovery, and complications across three fixation techniques, concluding the techniques were comparable. Targeted searches for jersey-finger or flexor-digitorum-profundus-avulsion contracture, stiffness, distal interphalangeal osteoarthritis, delayed-diagnosis complications, and complex regional pain syndrome returned no condition-specific quantification in this window.

Evidence-ground screen recorded 2026-09-24: the outcomes that the located studies do measure - total active motion, QuickDASH, Buck-Gramcko grading, grip and pinch strength, and loss of distal interphalangeal flexion - have no matching catalog identities (there is no loss-of-finger-flexion, grip-weakness, or hand-function identity), and the nearest structural targets require evidence the located literature does not provide: a contractures edge would need a reported incidence of distal interphalangeal joint contracture rather than an aggregate poor-outcome grade, and a post-traumatic-osteoarthritis edge would need documented degenerative joint change at the distal interphalangeal joint after the avulsion, which was not found. Direction guard: the causal arrows in the located literature run from the tendon avulsion to function and surgical technique rather than to a downstream disease, so authoring a generic unexplained-chronic-pain or loss-of-use edge would overstate the evidence. Reopening condition: a cohort reporting a catalog-fit secondary diagnosis after jersey finger, or a governance decision adding a functional-outcome identity for the hand.
